neurons in the dorsomedi hypothalamus mediate a diverse array of autonomic and neuro endocrine changes elicited from the preoptic region of the hypothalamus.
activity of neurons in dorsomedial hypothalamic (DMH) mediates diverse physiological responses evoked from medial preoptic area (MPOA).

activity of neurons in a brain region called the dorsomedial (DM) hypothalamus is necessary for physiological and behavioral responses evoked from another region called the medial preoptic (MPO) area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by the dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus (DMH) in the control of autonomic function.
the neural mechanisms that control autonomic, neurohormonal, and behavioral responses to stress and the role that these responses play in the pathophysiology of mood disorders.
elucidation of the neural mechanisms underlying autonomic, neurohormonal and behavioral responses evoked by activation of neurons in specific brain areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neurons in the dorsolateral preoptic area and the dorsomedial and lateral hypothalamus, as well as the paraventricular and ventromedial nuclei of the hypothalamus, all contribute to the autonomic, neurohumoral and locomotor responses to activation of neurons in medial preoptic area.
the DMH is the final common pathway for autonomic, neuro-endocrine, and locomotory responses evoked from preoptic area.
the dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus mediators the autonomic, neuro endocrine and locomotor responses from the medial pre-optic area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the medial preoptic and dorsomedial hypothalamic nuclei are reciprocally interconnected and that activity in neurons in the dorsolateral part of the dorsomedial nucleus mediates the autonomic and neurohormonal responses evoked from preoptic neurons.

the medial preoptic and dorsomedial hypothalamic areas form a functional unit that is critical for regulating a diverse array of autonomic and neurohormonal responses to a variety of physiological challenges and behavioral states.
the medial preoptic nucleus is the primary source of inhibition for the dorsomedial nucleus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dorsomedial region of the hypothalamus is an important site for the integration of physiological and behavioral changes evoked from a variety of brain sites.
the dorsomedial nucleus is a key site in the brain for integrating the effects of the preoptic area on the autonomic and endocrine systems.

the medial preoptic region represents an important inhibitory input to neurons in the dorsomedi hypothalamus, and that these neurons in turn control a diverse array of autonomic, neurohormonal, and behavioral changes in conscious rats.
